name: REA
works_with: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and other agents with local MCP
short: An MCP server that lets your agent reverse engineer apps, binaries and websites and show its evidence.
what: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, Android APKs, websites and more. You ask how a feature in an app works, and the agent traces it, explains it with evidence and can build a similar version. The same tools work from your terminal.
who: Developers and security researchers who want to understand how existing software works without its source. For native binaries you'll need Hopper, Ghidra or IDA, so it's not a casual install.
needs: Node.js 22.x (22.19 or later), 24.x (24.11 or later) or 26+, plus npm
For native binaries: Hopper, Ghidra or IDA. Setup can install Hopper if you approve
For websites: a Chrome-family browser. Other targets list their own tools in the README

steps.title: Set up your agent
steps.text: Choose your agents, review the proposed changes and approve them. It backs up your existing config. Restart your agent afterwards.

steps.title: Or try it from the terminal on an Electron app
steps.text: Replace the path with an extracted app folder or ASAR file.

steps.title: Keep it updated
steps.text: Releases come often. For the npm-installed CLI run `rea update`. If you set up with npx, run:

try.label: From the README
try.text:
Understand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a similar feature for my project.

(Swap Notes for the app and feature you care about.)

watch: Setup changes your agent's config to add REA's MCP server and its instructions. It shows the changes and keeps backups.
Runtime capture runs or interacts with the target app using your own user permissions. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection only read the files.
Analysis runs locally, but your agent sends the results to its model provider.
The README says you are responsible for having permission to reverse engineer a target and for following the law.
